subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Which owner boundary should drive the next step for this multi-agent Telegram/provider timeout report: current-main live reproduction first, targeted runtime/channel repair, or closure only after positive mitigation proof?
rationale: The evidence crosses Telegram runner concurrency, provider transport, model fallback, session/run timeouts, and launch defaults; choosing a code path without a current-main trace could add the wrong fallback or config policy.

options.title: Run Current-Main Live Repro First
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a four-agent Telegram trace on current main before selecting a code or config change.

options.title: Split Architecture Follow-Up
options.body: Use this issue as the symptom record and move broader provider/runtime pressure work to a separate canonical issue if maintainers choose that boundary.

options.title: Close After Positive Mitigation Proof
options.body: Close only if a current-main run shows the original simultaneous timeout pattern no longer occurs after the merged fallback mitigations.

recommendation.title: Run Current-Main Live Repro First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a four-agent Telegram trace on current main before selecting a code or config change.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the broadest recent history across fallback/provider architecture and is the best available owner for the cross-boundary product choice.
